_comment: RE-1 (docs/RECURRING_EVENTS_SPEC.md §5, §6.1, §16): the S14c moments block (tests/fixtures/moments_block.json, the deck as ruled) with the recurring deck under `affairs` — T1 the Arch-Chancellor's Letters, T2 the Host's Claims at two corps (P6), T3 Berthier's Memorial — exactly as §6.1 authors them, the counsel and echo lines from §12c. The shipped scenario authors no `affairs` key until RE-3 copies this deck into it; the engine pins arm the real booted world with this file.

deck.title: The Bavarian Match
deck.record: Eugène, adopted by Napoleon, wed Augusta of Bavaria at Munich (historically 14 January 1806); she had been promised to Baden's heir, and Munich yielded to the Emperor's pressing.

deck.title: The Throne of Holland

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Admiral Ver Huell, for the deputation of the States General

deck.record: Historically the Dutch deputation under Admiral Ver Huell asked Napoleon for a king and was given his brother Louis (5 June 1806); Grand Pensionary Schimmelpenninck resigned rather than sign. The alternative was annexation, 1810.

deck.title: The Crown of the Reich
deck.record: With the Confederation signed, Napoleon told Francis II to lay down the crown of the Holy Roman Empire (historically 22 July 1806); Francis did so on 6 August, and the Reich of a thousand years ended.

deck.title: The Decree of Berlin
deck.record: Historically, from Berlin after Jena (21 November 1806), Napoleon declared the British Isles in a state of blockade and shut every port of his allies to British goods.

deck.title: The Arch-Chancellor's Letters
deck.source: research #15 — Fondation Napoléon, "Walcheren et l'affaire Fouché": the Emperor's rebuke to Cambacérès for making so little use of his powers, August 1809; Malet's forged dispatch took Paris for a morning, 23 October 1812
deck.record: Historically the Emperor governed from his camp, and in August 1809 he rebuked Cambacérès for making so little use of the powers he had left him.
deck.watch: The Emperor afield: {n} of 6 mornings — Cambacérès may write.
deck.counsel: Berthier — Every hour you give the Council, Sire, is an hour the army waits for its orders.

accept.caption: Dictate from the field
accept.echo: Cambacérès: the Council has registered the decrees Your Majesty dictated from the field.

decline.caption: Let the Council act
decline.echo: Cambacérès: the Council has acted in Your Majesty's name; Paris will mark whose hand signed.

deck.title: The Host's Claims
deck.source: research #6 — Napoleon to Berthier, 14 July 1810 (Fondation Napoléon; Branda, Le prix de la gloire): war must feed war; a corps lived on the country it stood in
deck.record: Historically the Emperor's rule was that war must feed war (to Berthier, 14 July 1810): a corps lived on the country it stood in.
deck.watch: {n} corps on {host}'s soil: {m} of 3 mornings — its court may present its claims.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — An ally presents his bill once as an account, Sire. The second time, he presents it as a grievance.

accept.caption: Pay the host's claims
accept.echo: {minister}: the account between {host} and Paris is square for the season.

deck.title: Berthier's Memorial
deck.source: REFORMS_SPEC.md §6 — the law's own record, Berthier's Imperial Headquarters, expanded 1805–07; Berthier Major-General of the Grande Armée from 1805

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Berthier, Major-General of the Grande Armée

deck.record: Historically Berthier's Imperial Headquarters grew with every campaign from 1805 into the staff that carried the Emperor's orders.
deck.watch: At war {n} of 4 turns, and the chest could found the headquarters — Berthier may write.
deck.counsel: Daru — The Intendance can pay for clerks, Sire. It cannot pay for an order that reaches a corps a day late.

accept.caption: Found the headquarters
accept.echo: Berthier: the Imperial Headquarters is founded; the orders of the day go out under his seal.
